metadata.title: Parallel performance of peclet.flow 1.0.0: strong and weak scaling of a cut-cell immersed-boundary incompressible flow solver on Snellius (Genoa CPU, H100 GPU)
metadata.description:
Measurement data and reproduction scripts for the parallel performance of peclet.flow 1.0.0 solving creeping flow through a periodic random sphere packing with the cut-cell immersed boundary method.

One physical problem is measured on four ladders: weak scaling on 1–32 NVIDIA H100 GPUs at 3843 cells per GPU (56.6 M to 1.81 G cells), strong scaling of one fixed 56.6 M-cell problem on 24–1536 AMD Genoa cores and on 1–32 H100 GPUs, and a geometry-free Taylor–Green control on the same grids. The weak ladder tiles one unit cell, so every rung is an exact periodic replication of the same problem and the physical observable is a single number that every rung must reproduce — not a scatter across independently packed beds.

The record contains the driver, the geometry artifact and the script that generated it, the cluster provisioning and job scripts, the raw per-run JSON and logs, the analysis that produces the tables and figures, and a build census (toolchain, MPI, driver, wheel checksums) for every machine. The solver is configured at its shipped 1.0.0 defaults, with one stated exception documented in the report.

Addendum, 2026-09-15. A companion campaign re-ran the CPU strong-scaling ladder with the momentum solver pinned at every rank count instead of left to the solver's automatic rule, and recorded the momentum sweep count. It establishes that the red-black Gauss–Seidel momentum solve runs at its iteration cap on every rung of the CPU ladder, that the velocity multigrid is the faster momentum solver at every rank count measured (not only below the threshold at which 1.0.0 selects it), and that the CPU ladder's apparent above-ideal strong scaling is an artefact of the solver switching algorithm at its top rung. Three readings in the report are corrected accordingly and marked in place; no timing, efficiency or permeability value is revised. The companion campaign's raw results and scripts are archived in this record alongside the primary ones.

Runs were performed on the Dutch national supercomputer Snellius (SURF).
metadata.notes: Scripts in this record are MIT-licensed (as the peclet-examples repository); the measurement data are CC-BY-4.0. This record was amended on 2026-09-15 before publication: the measurements are unchanged and three interpretations were corrected, each marked in place in the report.
